title: Introduce Cost Snapper: adaptive burst-prefill and quant safety profiles
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: sudden traffic bursts cause inefficient cold KV/cache behavior and poor unit economics. Cost Snapper implements an adaptive burst-prefill admission policy plus conservative quantization safety profiles to reduce per-token cost while protecting output quality. This PR introduces a lightweight sampled admission controller that opportunistically triggers prefill inflations during short burst windows, a shadow-run simulator to validate unit-econ impact, and a set of conservative quant safety fences for models with fragile output fidelity. Key goals: reduce token spend on cold starts, avoid regressions in quality for critical prompts, and provide operator controls for rollout. Changes include a runtime policy, a simulator harness, telemetry and console knobs, and SDK helpers. Checklist: [x] design doc linked (linear/ENG-1982) [x] unit tests added [x] integration smoke tests in canary [x] docs/console updates [x] rollout plan (canary -> 10% -> 50% -> global) Rollout notes: default disabled for customers; enabled by opt-in flag in console or via api config to avoid surprise changes in unit costs. Metrics to watch: token-cost-per-request, prefill-hit-rate, kv-cache-warmup-time, quality-regression-alerts. Related: ENG-1982, PM-453, SUP-1209.

release_notes: Add 'Cost Snapper' experimental feature: adaptive burst-prefill admission policy and conservative quantization safety profiles. Opt-in via console flag; expected token-cost reduction on bursty workloads of ~10-20% in early A/B tests. Monitor econ metrics after enabling.
notes: This PR intentionally ships conservative defaults: prefill thresholds are narrow and quant safety profiles avoid aggressive lower-bit quant for models marked 'fragile'. Operator experience: toggle in Console -> Inference Controls -> Prefill, and view cost impact in Console -> Econ dashboards. Follow the rollout doc in docs/ops/rollouts.md for canary steps.
